And the clause «تبتغوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second implied particle-relative (أن).
And the clause «لعلّكم تشكرون ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal, and is conjoined to the preceding causal clause for which the lām is used [Note: or conjoined to an implied preceding causal clause, i.e. "so that you may perceive His bounty and so that you may give thanks".].
And the clause «تشكرون» is in the position of the nominative, khabar of laʿalla.
(الواو): conjunctive. (ألقى): a past verb, indeclinable on an implied fatḥa on the alif. (في الأرض): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ألقى), which is given the sense of "created". (رواسي): direct object, accusative — an adjective of an omitted qualified noun, i.e. "firm mountains" — and tanwīn is withheld because it is a plural of the form of the ultimate plurals (muntahā al-jumūʿ). (أن): a maṣdar particle and accusative. (تميد): an imperfect verb, accusative; the agent is "she". (الباء): a preposition, and (كم) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (تميد).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تميد) is in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl li-ajlihi, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "for fear that it would sway with you". (الواو): conjunctive in the two places. (أنهارا، سبلا): two nouns conjoined to رواسي, accusative like it. (لعلّكم تهتدون): like لعلّكم تشكرون.
The clause «ألقى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause سخّر البحر.
And the clause «لعلّكم تهتدون» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption — or causal.
And the clause «تهتدون» is in the position of the nominative, khabar of laʿalla.
(الواو): conjunctive. (علامات): conjoined to رواسي, accusative like it, its accusative marker being the kasra. (الواو): resumptive. (بالنجم): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يهتدون). (هم): a detached pronoun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ. (يهتدون): like تلبسون.
The clause «هم يهتدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «يهتدون» is in the position of the nominative, khabar.

* Morphology:
(طريّا): a resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from طرو يطرو (the pattern of كرم) and طري يطري (the pattern of فرح). If it comes from the pattern of كرم, it has an i'lāl by substitution: its origin is طريو, with a wāw and a preceding yāʾ that is sākin; the wāw was turned into a yāʾ and assimilated into the first yāʾ, so it became طريّ on the wazn فعيل.
(مواخر): plural of ماخرة, feminine of ماخر, an active participle of مخر البحر, i.e. it ran in it and cleaved it. The wazn of مواخر is فواعل.
(علامات): plural of علامة, a noun for a sign, from أعلمت على كذا in a book and elsewhere. Its wazn is فعالة (fatḥa on the fāʾ).

* Rhetoric:
1- Completion (tatmīm): in His saying, Exalted is He, لِتَأْكُلُوا مِنْهُ لَحْماً طَرِيًّا, there is a tatmīm of precaution. Tatmīm is an art involving a word which, if dropped from the speech, would reduce its meaning. It is of three kinds: tatmīm of deficiency, tatmīm of precaution, and tatmīm of exaggeration. We say here that He, Glorified is He, knew that if He did not describe the meat as fresh it would not be liable to spoil; yet it is well known that spoilage reaches fresh meat more than other kinds, so it was necessary to describe it as such so that one would hasten to eat it for fear of its spoiling.
2- Shift of person (iltifāt): in His saying, Exalted is He, وَبِالنَّجْمِ هُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ, the speech is taken out of the course of direct address, and the preposing of the preposition and its noun and the pronoun is for specification, as if it were said: "by the star in particular, these in particular are guided"; so taking heed of that, and giving thanks for it through affirming oneness, is more binding upon them and more obligatory for them.

safi-cedvel:17-17.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة): for rebuking interrogation. (الفاء): resumptive. (من): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ. (يخلق): an imperfect verb, nominative; the agent is a latent pronoun (huwa), which is the returning pronoun. (الكاف): a preposition. (من): a relative noun in the position of the genitive, attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. (لا): negative. (يخلق): like the first. (الهمزة): like the first. (الفاء): conjunctive. (لا): like the first. (تذكّرون): an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the agent.
The clause «من يخلق كمن لا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «يخلق ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
And the clause «لا يخلق ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من) (the second).
And the clause «تذكّرون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive [Note: or conjoined to an implied preceding resumptive, i.e. "Were you ignorant of this, so do you not remember?"].

* Rhetoric:
1- Reversed simile (tashbīh maqlūb): this is in His saying, Exalted is He, أَفَمَنْ يَخْلُقُ كَمَنْ لا يَخْلُقُ, for the apparent requirement is the reverse of it, because the address is to the worshippers of idols, who called them gods in likeness to Him, Exalted is He, so they made the one who does not create like the Creator. The address therefore came in opposition to this, as though, owing to their exaggeration in worshipping them, their baseness and, consequently, the overturning of their minds, the idols had become for them the original, and the true Creator had become the secondary term; so the rebuke came in accordance with that.
2- Predominance (taghlīb): in the noble verse, where "man" is used, giving predominance to those possessed of knowledge over others, with the matching (mushākala) that this contains; or it refers to those possessed of knowledge specifically, and the state of others is known from it by the indication of the text, for if one who creates is not like one who does not create, and the latter is among those possessed of knowledge, what do you think of inanimate things?
So what is meant by "the one who does not create" is the idols, and "man", which is for rational beings possessed of knowledge, was used because, when they worshipped them and called them gods, they treated them as those possessed of knowledge, so "man" was brought according to their belief and in accordance with what is ingrained in their natures.

* Benefits:
1- Among the curiosities of the jurists is that they say: if a man swears not to eat meat and then eats fish, he does not break his oath. If an objector objects to them that Allah the Exalted called it meat, they say: the matter is based on custom, and the custom of people is that when meat is mentioned in the absolute, fish is not understood from it. They said: do you not see that if he swears not to ride an animal (dābba) and then rides a disbeliever, he does not break his oath, even though Allah called him a dābba in His saying: إِنَّ شَرَّ الدَّوَابِّ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا — and so on through these discussions, which are referred to in the longer books of fiqh.
2- Writing the hamza:
a- The rule in writing the hamza is that it is written on the letter to which it would be eased if it were lightened. Lightening is permissible in Arabic, so you say: سال, قرا, لولو, ذياب, خطيّة, ميّة, etc.
b- The initial hamza: it is only ever vowelled and pronounced with full articulation, and it must be written in the form of the alif whatever vowel it has.
Such as: أمل, إبل, أحد.
c- The final hamza at the end of the word.
What precedes it is either sākin or vowelled:
1- If what precedes it is sākin, it is written on the line, such as المرء, الجزء, الخبء, المقروء, الشيء, النوء.
2- If what precedes it is vowelled, it is written on a letter that suits the vowel of what precedes it, as in: الخطأ, والتواطؤ, ويستهزئ.
c- The medial hamza:
If it is sākin, it is written on a letter that suits the vowel of the letter before it, such as رأس, سؤل, بئر; and if it is vowelled, it is written on a letter that corresponds to the vowel of the stronger of it and the letter before it, such as: سأل, سئم, تؤجج, خؤون, فئات.
There are exceptions to these general rules which we pass over without mention, fearing prolixity and departure from the plan of the book.

safi-cedvel:18-21.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive. (إن): a jussive conditional particle. (تعدّوا): an imperfect verb, jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its jussive marker being the omission of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the agent. (نعمة): direct object, accusative. (الله): the word of majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (لا): negative. (تحصوها): like تعدّوا, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).. and (ها) is a pronoun, direct object. (إنّ): a particle of emphasis and accusative. (الله): the word of majesty, the noun of inna, accusative. (اللام): the shifted lām, for emphasis. (غفور): the khabar of inna, nominative. (رحيم): a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «إن تعدّوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «لا تحصوها ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a jussive condition, not accompanied by the fāʾ. And the clause «إنّ الله لغفور ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
(الواو): conjunctive. (الله): the word of majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative. (يعلم): an imperfect verb, nominative; the agent is a latent pronoun (huwa). (ما): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative, direct object; the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "تسرّونه" [Note: It is permissible for (ما) to be a maṣdar particle, with the interpreted maṣdar as direct object..]. (تسرّون): an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the agent. (الواو): conjunctive. (ما تعلنون): like ما تسرّون.
The clause «الله يعلم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إن تعدّوا ...
And the clause «يعلم ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
And the clause «تسرّون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the first relative noun (ما).
And the clause «تعلنون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
(الواو): conjunctive. (الّذين): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ. (يدعون): like تسرّون. (من دون): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun. (الله): the word of majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (لا): negative. (يخلقون): like تسرّون. (شيئا): direct object, accusative. (الواو): circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (هم): a detached pronoun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ. (يخلقون): a passive imperfect verb.. and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «الّذين يدعون..» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause الله يعلم.
And the clause «يدعون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين).
And the clause «لا يخلقون شيئا ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الّذين).
And the clause «يخلقون» is in the position of the nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
And the clause «هم يخلقون» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl [Note: or in the position of the nominative, conjoined by the wāw to the clause (لا يخلقون..).].
(أموات): a second khabar for the mubtadaʾ (هم) [Note: or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هم", and the clause is resumptive.], nominative. (غير): naʿt of أموات, nominative, and it gave emphasis. (أحياء): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الواو): conjunctive. (ما): negative. (يشعرون): like تسرّون. (أيّان): an interrogative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative as an adverb of time, attached to (يبعثون), which is like يخلقون in being passive.
The clause «ما يشعرون» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause يخلقون (the khabar).
And the clause «يبعثون ... » is in the position of the accusative, direct object of the verb يشعرون, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative أيّان ... or by removal of the preposition.

* Benefits:
- أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ.
"Ayyāna" comes without "mā" and comes joined to it. In both cases it is a jussive conditional noun of time.
a- Bare, as in:
أيان نؤمنك تأمن غيرنا وإذا ... لم تدرك الأمن منا لم تزل حذرا
(Whenever we give you security you are safe from others; and if you do not attain security from us, you will not cease being wary.)
b- Joined to "mā", as in:
إذا ما النعجة الأدماء باتت بقفرة ... فأيان ما تعدل به الريح تنزل
(When the dark-hued ewe spends the night in a wasteland, wherever the wind turns her, she will alight.)
Remark: "ayyāna" may be an interrogative noun about time, and it is compounded of two words, "ayy" and "ān".

safi-cedvel:22-22.t:
* I'rab:
(إلهكم): mubtadaʾ, nominative.. and (كم) is the muḍāf ilayhi. (إله): khabar, nominative. (واحد): naʿt of إله, nominative. (الفاء): resumptive. (الذين): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ. (لا): negative. (يؤمنون): an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the agent. (بالآخرة): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يؤمنون). (قلوبهم): mubtadaʾ, nominative.. and (هم) is the muḍāf ilayhi. (منكرة): khabar, nominative. (الواو): conjunctive. (هم): a pronoun in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ. (مستكبرون): khabar, nominative, its nominative marker being the wāw.
The clause «إلهكم إله واحد» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «الّذين لا يؤمنون ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «لا يؤمنون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين).
And the clause «قلوبهم منكرة ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الّذين).
And the clause «هم مستكبرون» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause قلوبهم منكرة [Note: It is permissible for it to be circumstantial, in which case it is in the position of the accusative.].

* Morphology:
(مستكبرون): plural of مستكبر, an active participle of استكبر, the six-letter verb. Its wazn is مستفعل (ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn).

safi-cedvel:23-23.t:
* I'rab:
(لا): the lā of generic negation. (جرم): the noun of lā, indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of the accusative [Note: See verse (22) of sūrat Hūd, for the i'rab of (لا جرم) has further explanation there.]. (أنّ): a particle of emphasis and accusative. (الله): the word of majesty, the noun of anna, accusative. (يعلم): an imperfect verb, nominative; the agent is a latent pronoun (huwa). (ما يسرّون وما يعلنون): their i'rab has been given before [Note: in verse (19) of this sūra.].
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله يعلم..) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, i.e. "no doubt that Allah..", attached to the khabar of lā. (إنّه): a particle of emphasis and accusative.. and (الهاء) is a pronoun, the noun of inna. (لا): negative. (يحبّ): like يعلم. (المستكبرين): direct object, accusative, its accusative marker being the yāʾ.
The clause «لا جرم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «يعلم ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of anna.
And the clause «يسرّون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the first relative noun (ما).
And the clause «يعلنون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
And the clause «إنّه لا يحبّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «لا يحبّ ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of inna.

safi-cedvel:24-24.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive. (إذا): an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, indeclinable in the position of the accusative, attached to (قالوا). (قيل): a passive past verb. (اللام): a preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (قيل). (ما): an interrogative noun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ. (ذا): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, khabar [Note: or (ماذا) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative, direct object, its governor being أنزل.]. (أنزل): a past verb. (ربّكم): agent, nominative.. and (كم) is the muḍāf ilayhi; the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "أنزله". (قالوا): a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and (الواو) is the agent. (أساطير): the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "المنزل" ("what is sent down") [Note: or "what you claim to have been sent down"]. (الأوّلين): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its genitive marker being the yāʾ.
The clause «قيل ... » is in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «ماذا أنزل ... » is in the position of the nominative, nāʾib fāʿil [Note: because it is originally a clause of the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl), and according to the majority it is an explanation of the implied nāʾib fāʿil, i.e. "the saying was said ..."].
And the clause «أنزل ربّكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ذا).
And the clause «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause « (المنزل) أساطير ... » is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech.

safi-cedvel:25-25.t:
* [Note: See the i'rab of the last part of the verse in sūrat al-Anʿām (verse 31).]
I'rab:
(اللام): the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba). (يحملوا): an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, its accusative marker being the omission of the nūn ... and (الواو) is the agent. (أوزارهم): direct object, accusative.. and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (كاملة): an accusative ḥāl from أوزار. (يوم): an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يحملوا). (القيامة): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يحملوا ... ) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (قالوا) [Note: in the preceding verse (24) .. Ibn ʿAṭiyya, however, attached it to an omitted verb, its implied form being "He decreed that so that they bear their burdens", and in his view the lām is for causation.].
(الواو): conjunctive. (من أوزار): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يحملوا), and من is partitive. (الّذين): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi. (يضلّونهم): an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the agent, and (هم) is the direct object. (بغير): a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl from the agent of يضلّون or from its object, according to how the meaning is construed. (علم): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (ألا): a particle of alerting. (ساء): a past verb for expressing blame (inshāʾ al-dhamm); the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa". (ما): an indefinite noun, tamyīz (specification) of the agent, in the position of the accusative. (يزرون): like يضلّون.
The clause «يحملوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
And the clause «يضلّونهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين).
And the clause «ساء ما يزرون ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «يزرون ... » is in the position of the accusative, naʿt of (ما).

safi-cedvel:26-29.t:
* I'rab:
(قد): a particle of verification. (مكر): a past verb. (الذين): a relative noun in the position of the nominative, agent. (من قبلهم): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila of the relative noun..
and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الفاء): conjunctive. (أتى): a past verb, indeclinable on an implied fatḥa. (الله): the word of majesty, agent, nominative, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the command of Allah came". (بنيانهم): direct object, accusative.. and (هم) is like the last. (من القواعد): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أتى), i.e. from the side of the foundations. (الفاء): conjunctive. (خرّ): like مكر. (على): a preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (خرّ). (السقف): agent, nominative. (من فوقهم): a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl from السقف, and it is an emphasis of what precedes it, and (هم) is like the last. (الواو): conjunctive. (أتاهم): like the first.. and (هم) is a pronoun, direct object. (العذاب): agent, nominative. (من): a preposition. (حيث): a noun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of the genitive, attached to (أتاهم). (لا): negative. (يشعرون): an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the agent.
The clause «مكر الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «أتى الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive.
And the clause «خرّ عليهم السقف ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أتى الله..
And the clause «أتاهم العذاب ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أتى الله ...
And the clause «لا يشعرون ... » is in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
(ثمّ): a conjunction. (يوم): an adverb, accusative, attached to (يخزيهم). (القيامة): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (يخزيهم): an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marker being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ, and (هم) is a pronoun, direct object, and the agent is a latent pronoun (huwa). (الواو): conjunctive. (يقول): like يخزي, its nominative marker being the overt ḍamma. (أين): an interrogative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, attached to a preposed khabar. (شركائي): postposed mubtadaʾ, its nominative marker being the ḍamma implied on the letter before the yāʾ ... and (الياء) is the muḍāf ilayhi. (الّذين): a relative noun in the position of the nominative, naʿt of شركاء. (كنتم): a defective past verb, a naskh verb.. and (تم) is a pronoun in the position of the nominative, the noun of kāna. (تشاقّون): like يشعرون. (في): a preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to the verb تشاقّون. (قال): like مكر. (الّذين): a relative noun, agent. (أوتوا): a passive past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil. (العلم): direct object, accusative. (إنّ): a particle resembling the verb, a naskh particle. (الخزي): the noun of inna, accusative. (اليوم): an adverb of time, accusative, attached to الخزي. (الواو): conjunctive. (السوء): conjoined to الخزي, accusative. (على الكافرين): a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar of inna, its genitive marker being the yāʾ.
The clause «يخزيهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause مكر الذين ...
And the clause «يقول ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يخزيهم.
And the clause «أين شركائي ... » is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech.
And the clause «كنتم تشاقّون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين).
And the clause «تشاقّون فيهم» is in the position of the accusative, khabar of كنتم.
And the clause «قال الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause «أوتوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «إنّ الخزي.. على الكافرين» is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech.
(الّذين): a relative noun in the position of the genitive, naʿt of الكافرين [Note: or in the position of the nominative, the khabar of an obligatorily omitted mubtadaʾ in the manner of blame, its implied form being "هم".. and according to the school of al-Akhfash it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause ألقوا, with the fāʾ added because the mubtadaʾ resembles a condition.]. (تتوفّاهم): an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marker being the ḍamma implied on the alif.. and (هم) is a pronoun, direct object. (الملائكة): agent, nominative. (ظالمي): an accusative ḥāl from the object pronoun, its accusative marker being the yāʾ. (أنفسهم): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.. and (هم) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (الفاء): resumptive — or conjunctive. (ألقوا): a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma implied on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two sākin letters.. and (الواو) is the agent. (السّلم): direct object, accusative. (ما): negative. (كنّا): a defective past verb.. and (نا) is the noun of kāna. (نعمل): an imperfect verb, nominative; the agent is "we". (من): a redundant preposition. (سوء): genitive in form, accusative in position, direct object. (بلى): a particle of response. (إنّ الله): like إنّ الخزي. (عليم): the khabar of inna, nominative. (الباء): a preposition. (ما): a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "تعملونه", and the clause after it is the ṣila.
Or it is conjoined to the ṣila clause — تتوفّاهم.. It is said that it is conjoined to the clause هم الذين.. if the relative noun is parsed as a khabar.]. (كنتم تعملون): like كنتم تشاقّون.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كنتم تعملون) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (عليم).
And the clause «تتوفّاهم الملائكة ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين).
And the clause «ألقوا السلم» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «ما كنّا نعمل ... » is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech of an implied saying [Note: or explicative of السلم if it is in the sense of speech, in which case it has no grammatical position.].
And the clause «نعمل من سوء ... » is in the position of the accusative, khabar of كنّا.
And the clause «إنّ الله عليم ... » is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech of an implied saying. And the clause «كنتم تعملون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما). And the clause «تعملون» is in the position of the accusative, khabar of كنتم.
(الفاء): conjunctive, linking the effect with the cause. (ادخلوا): an imperative verb, indeclinable on the omission of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the agent. (أبواب): direct object, accusative. (جهنّم): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its genitive marker being the fatḥa. (خالدين): an accusative ḥāl from the agent of ادخلوا, its accusative marker being the yāʾ. (في): a preposition, and (ها) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to خالدين. (الفاء): resumptive. (اللام): the lām of emphasis. (بئس): an inert past verb for expressing blame. (مثوى): agent, nominative, its nominative marker being the ḍamma implied on the alif. (المتكبّرين): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its genitive marker being the yāʾ; and the one specified for blame is omitted, its implied form being "هي", i.e. Jahannam.
The clause «ادخلوا ... » is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause of the quoted speech إنّ الله عليم..
And the clause «لبئس مثوى ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(السقف): an inert noun for what faces the ground in a house. Its plural is سقوف (ḍamma on the sīn) and سقف (two ḍammas).
(المتكبّرين): plural of المتكبّر, an active participle of تكبّر, the five-letter verb. Its wazn is متفعّل (ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn).

* Rhetoric:
(1) Representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): in His saying, Exalted is He, قَدْ مَكَرَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ فَأَتَى اللَّهُ بُنْيانَهُمْ مِنَ الْقَواعِدِ فَخَرَّ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّقْفُ مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ — the speech is a representation (tamthīl). It means that their state in arranging the snares and stratagems with which to plot against the messengers of Allah, Exalted is He, peace be upon them, and Allah's, Exalted is He, nullifying them and making them the cause of their destruction, is like the state of a people who built a structure and propped it with columns, and it was struck from the side of its columns, which were shaken, so the roof fell upon them and they perished beneath it. The point of resemblance is that what they set up and imagined as a cause of fortification and mastery became a cause of ruin and annihilation. The columns are in the position of the snares set up, and their overturning upon them is a destruction like the overturning of those stratagems upon their authors; and the structure is what they had fabricated and in which they pinned hope upon those snares, and bowed beneath it from an opinion buttressed by schemes. It resembles their saying: "Whoever digs a pit for his brother falls into it headlong."
2- Precaution (iḥtirās): in His saying, Exalted is He, فَخَرَّ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّقْفُ مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ — for someone may say: a roof is only ever from above, so what is the meaning of mentioning "from above them"? The answer is that it is a precaution against the possibility that the roof might be a floor with respect to others, for many roofs are floors for some people and roofs for others; so Allah, Exalted is He, removed this possibility with two expressions, namely His saying "upon them" and His saying "kharra" (fell), because the latter is only used for what descends or falls from above to below.

* Benefits:
- Balā: a particle of response, specific to refuting a negation, whether a pure negation, as in زَعَمَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنْ لَنْ يُبْعَثُوا قُلْ: بَلى وَرَبِّي لَتُبْعَثُنَّ,
or a negation joined to a genuine interrogative, as in «أليس عليّ بآت» [Translator's note: the example is printed thus in the source; the form «عليّ» looks like a misprint, but it is translated as written.] and the answer is: balā..
or to an interrogative that has departed from its true sense to rebuke, as in أَمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّا لا نَسْمَعُ سِرَّهُمْ وَنَجْواهُمْ بَلى; or to affirmation, as in His saying, Exalted is He: أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قالُوا: بَلى..
The difference between balā and naʿam is that balā only comes after a negation, whereas naʿam comes after both negation and affirmation!

safi-cedvel:30-30.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive. (قيل.. ماذا أنزل ربّكم قالوا): their i'rab has been given before [Note: in verse (24) of this sūra. The most appropriate view of (ماذا) is that it is one noun in the position of the accusative, direct object, because the clause of the answer is verbal — i.e. "He sent down good" — so that there is a correspondence between the question and the answer.]. (اللام): a preposition. (الّذين): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the genitive, attached to (قيل). (ألقوا): like اتقوا [Note: in verse (28) of this sūra.]. (خيرا): direct object of an omitted verb, i.e. "He sent down good". (للّذين): like the first, attached to a preposed khabar. (أحسنوا): a past verb and its agent. (في): a preposition. (ها): a particle of alerting. (ذه): a demonstrative, indeclinable in the position of the genitive, attached to (أحسنوا). (الدنيا): badal from ذه, following it in the genitive, its genitive marker being the kasra implied on the alif. (حسنة): postposed mubtadaʾ, nominative. (الواو): conjunctive. (اللام): the lām of inceptive. (دار): mubtadaʾ, nominative. (الآخرة): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (خير): khabar, nominative. (الواو): conjunctive. (اللام): the lām of emphasis. (نعم): an inert past verb for expressing praise. (دار): agent, nominative. (المتّقين): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its genitive marker being the yāʾ; and the one specified for praise is omitted, its implied form being "هي", i.e. the abode of the Hereafter.
The clause «قيل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «اتّقوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «أنزل ربّكم ... » is in the position of the nominative, nāʾib fāʿil [Note: See note (2) on page (34).. It is permissible for the clause to be the ṣila of (ذا), the khabar, and for the clause ماذا to be the nāʾib fāʿil.].
And the clause «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause « (أنزل) خيرا ... » is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech.
And the clause «للذين أحسنوا.. حسنة» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption [Note: al-Zamakhsharī made it a badal from (خيرا), as a report of the saying of those who were God-fearing ...].
And the clause «أحسنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «لدار الآخرة خير» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause للذين أحسنوا.
And the clause «لنعم دار المتّقين» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause دار الآخرة خير [Note: or it is the answer to an implied oath.].

safi-cedvel:31-32.t:
* I'rab:
(جنّات): the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هي" [Note: or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause يدخلونها, or an implied "لهم".]. (عدن): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (يدخلونها): an imperfect verb, nominative, and (الواو) is the agent, and (ها) is a pronoun, direct object. (تجري): an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marker being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ. (من تحتها): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تجري) [Note: or attached to an omitted ḥāl from الأنهار.], and it contains an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "from beneath its houses or its trees".. and (ها) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (الأنهار): agent of تجري, nominative. (اللام): a preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a preposed khabar. (فيها): like لهم, attached to the khabar. (ما): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, postposed mubtadaʾ. (يشاءون): an imperfect verb, nominative..
and (الواو) is the agent. (الكاف): a preposition of likeness [Note: or it is a noun meaning "like", in the position of the accusative as an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) substituting for the maṣdar, so it is a naʿt of it.. or a ḥāl from the pronoun of the maṣdar, or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "the matter is thus"..]. (ذلك): a demonstrative, indeclinable in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted absolute object whose governor is يجزي, the reference being to the recompense, and (اللام) denotes distance, and (الكاف) is for address. (يجزي الله): like تجري الأنهار. (المتّقين): direct object, accusative, its accusative marker being the yāʾ.
The clause « (هي) جنّات ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «يدخلونها ... » is in the position of the nominative, naʿt of جنّات.
And the clause «تجري.. الأنهار» is in the position of the accusative, ḥāl from the third-person pronoun in (يدخلونها).
And the clause «لهم فيها ما يشاءون» is in the position of the accusative, ḥāl from the agent pronoun of يدخلونها or from its object.
And the clause «يشاءون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause «يجزي الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
(الّذين تتوفّاهم الملائكة): their i'rab has been given before [Note: in verse (28) of this sūra.]. (طيّبين): an accusative ḥāl from the object of تتوفّاهم. (يقولون): like يدخلون. (سلام): mubtadaʾ, nominative [Note: It was permissible for it to be a mubtadaʾ though indefinite because it has the sense of a supplication.]. (على): a preposition, and (كم) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. (أدخلوا الجنة): like ادخلوا أبواب.. [Note: in verse (29) of this sūra.]. (بما كنتم تعملون): its i'rab has been given before [Note: in verse (28) of this sūra.].
And the clause «تتوفّاهم الملائكة ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «يقولون ... » is in the position of the accusative, ḥāl from الملائكة.
And the clause «سلام عليكم» is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech.
And the clause «ادخلوا الجنّة ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the saying.
And the clause «كنتم تعملون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the nominal or particle-relative (ما).
And the clause «تعملون» is in the position of the accusative, khabar of كنتم.

safi-cedvel:33-34.t:
* I'rab:
(هل): an interrogative particle containing the sense of negation. (ينظرون): an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the agent. (إلّا): for restriction. (أن): a maṣdar particle and accusative. (تأتيهم): an imperfect verb, accusative.. and (هم) is a pronoun, direct object. (الملائكة): agent, nominative. (أو): a conjunction. (يأتي): like the first, and conjoined to it. (أمر): agent, nominative. (ربّك): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.. and (الكاف) is a muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تأتيهم ... ) is in the position of the accusative, direct object, its governor being ينظرون. (كذلك فعل الذين): like كذلك يجزي الله [Note: in the preceding verse (31).. Here it is limited to attaching the kāf to an omitted absolute object whose governor is the verb.]. (من قبلهم): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative noun الذين ... and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو): resumptive. (ما): negative. (ظلمهم): a past verb.. and (هم) is the direct object. (الله): the word of majesty, agent, nominative. (الواو): conjunctive. (لكن): a particle of correction (istidrāk). (كانوا): a defective past verb, a naskh verb, and the wāw is its noun. (أنفس): preposed direct object, accusative, and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (يظلمون): like ينظرون.
The clause «هل ينظرون ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «تأتيهم الملائكة ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن), and the clause «يأتي أمر ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تأتيهم..
And the clause «فعل الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «ما ظلمهم الله» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: It is permissible for the clause to be circumstantial after the wāw of ḥāl..].
And the clause «كانوا ... يظلمون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ما ظلمهم الله.
And the clause «يظلمون» is in the position of the accusative, khabar of كانوا.
(الفاء): conjunctive. (أصابهم سيّئات): like ظلمهم الله. (ما): a maṣdar particle. (عملوا): a past verb and its agent.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما عملوا ... ) is in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
(الواو): conjunctive. (حاق): a past verb. (الباء): a preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (حاق). (ما): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, agent [Note: or a maṣdar particle, with the interpreted maṣdar as agent, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the recompense of their mockery".]. (كانوا ... يستهزئون): like كانوا يظلمون. (به): like بهم, attached to (يستهزئون).
The clause «أصابهم سيّئات ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ما ظلمهم الله [Note: or conjoined to the clause فعل الذين.. if the clause ما ظلمهم الله is parsed as a ḥāl.].
And the clause «حاق بهم ما كانوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أصابهم.
And the clause «كانوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause «يستهزئون» is in the position of the accusative, khabar of كانوا.

* Benefits:
1- The Qur'anic composition (al-naẓm al-qur'ānī):
Everyone who has been given a share of taste and an aptitude for the art perceives, with a conscious and deep perception, what a great role preposing and postposing play in realising the Qur'anic composition and the musical resonance it contains. Look at His saying, Exalted is He: لكِنْ كانُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ — how the object «أنفسهم» was preposed before the verb يظلمون, and note the effect of that in realising the point of focus of the verse. Likewise His saying, Exalted is He: وَحاقَ بِهِمْ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ — where «به» was preposed before the verb for the same purpose. This observation is worthy of study at the level of the Book of Allah as a whole, in order to show the dimensions of this characteristic and the means that combined to realise this aim.
2- The relation of the ḥāl to time: if we examined all that occurs in the Book of Allah or elsewhere of forms of the ḥāl, we would find that, in respect of its relation to time, it does not go beyond three cases: 1- either the ḥāl's occurrence coincides with its time, as in: هذا بَعْلِي شَيْخاً.
2- or its occurrence is considered to be in the future, as in: فَادْخُلُوها خالِدِينَ.
3- or it is narrated from the past, as in: "Khālid came yesterday riding."
And His saying, Exalted is He, سَلامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ oscillates between the present and the future, that is, between this world and the Hereafter; so both views are permissible.

safi-cedvel:35-35.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive. (قال): a past verb. (الذين): a relative noun, agent. (أشركوا): a past verb and its agent. (لو): a non-jussive conditional particle. (شاء): like قال. (الله): the word of majesty, agent, nominative. (ما): negative. (عبدنا): a past verb and its agent. (من دونه): a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl from شيء.. and (الهاء) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (من): a redundant preposition. (شيء): genitive in form, accusative in position, direct object. (نحن): a detached pronoun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, tawkīd of the first-person pronoun نا. (الواو): conjunctive. (لا): redundant, to emphasise the negation. (آباؤنا): conjoined to the first-person agent pronoun ... and (نا) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو): conjunctive. (حرّمنا من دونه من شيء): like عبدنا من ... من شيء. (كذلك.. من قبلهم): their i'rab has been given before [Note: in verse (33) of this sūra.]. (الفاء): resumptive. (هل): an interrogative particle in the sense of negation. (على الرسل): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to a preposed khabar. (إلّا): a particle of restriction. (البلاغ): postposed mubtadaʾ, nominative. (المبين): naʿt of البلاغ, nominative.
The clause «قال الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «أشركوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «لو شاء الله ... » is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech.
And the clause «ما عبدنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause «حرّمنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the apodosis clause.
And the clause «فعل الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «هل على الرسل إلّا البلاغ» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

safi-cedvel:36-36.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive. (اللام): the lām of an oath, for an implied oath. (قد): a particle of verification. (بعثنا): a past verb and its agent. (في كلّ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (بعثنا). (أمّة): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (رسولا): direct object, accusative. (أن): a particle of explanation, because بعثنا is in the sense of "We said".. [Note: It is permissible for (أن) to be a maṣdar particle, with the interpreted maṣdar in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, i.e. "with: worship..", and the preposition and its noun are attached to (بعثنا).]. (اعبدوا): an imperative verb, indeclinable on the omission of the nūn ... and (الواو) is the agent. (الله): the word of majesty, direct object, accusative. (الواو): conjunctive. (اجتنبوا الطاغوت): like اعبدوا الله. (الفاء): conjunctive, expressing ramification. (من): a preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a preposed khabar. (من): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, postposed mubtadaʾ [Note: or it is an indefinite noun in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ.]. (هدى): a past verb, indeclinable on an implied fatḥa. (الله): the word of majesty, agent, nominative. (الواو): conjunctive. (منهم من حقّت.. الضلالة): "منهم من هدى الله", and (التاء) is for the feminine. (على): a preposition, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of ..., attached to (حقّت) [Translator's note: the source text is incomplete here, giving "في محلّ" without "جرّ"; translated as written.]. (الفاء): linking the apodosis of an implied condition. (سيروا): like اعبدوا. (في الأرض): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (سيروا) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from the agent of سيروا, i.e. "reflecting or taking heed in the earth".]. (الفاء): conjunctive. (انظروا): like اعبدوا. (كيف): an interrogative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative, the khabar of the defective verb كان. (عاقبة): the noun of كان, nominative. (المكذّبين): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive ...
The clause «بعثنا..» has no grammatical position; it is the answer to an implied oath.. and the clause of the implied oath has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «اعبدوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative.
And the clause «اجتنبوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the explicative.
And the clause «منهم من هدى الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "so they were of divisions, and some of them are those whom..".
And the clause «هدى الله» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the first relative noun (من) [Note: or it is in the position of the nominative, naʿt of the qualified indefinite (من).].
And the clause «منهم من حقّت ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause منهم من هدى الله.
And the clause «حقّت عليه الضلالة..» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (من).
And the clause «سيروا ... » is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you want proof and certainty, then travel".
And the clause «انظروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause سيروا.
And the clause «كان عاقبة ... » is in the position of the accusative, direct object of the verb of looking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.

safi-cedvel:37-37.t:
* I'rab:
(إن): a jussive conditional particle. (تحرص): a jussive imperfect verb, the protasis; the agent is "you". (على هداهم): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تحرص), its genitive marker being the kasra implied on the alif.. and (هم) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (الفاء): causal. (إنّ): a particle resembling the verb. (الله): the word of majesty, the noun of inna, accusative. (لا): negative. (يهدي): an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marker being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ.. and the agent is a latent pronoun (huwa). (من): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative, direct object; the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "يضلّه". (يضلّ): an imperfect verb, nominative; the agent is "He", i.e. Allah. (الواو): conjunctive. (ما): negative. (اللام): a preposition. (هم): a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a preposed khabar. (من): a redundant preposition. (ناصرين): genitive in form, nominative in position, postposed mubtadaʾ.
The clause «تحرص ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «إنّ الله لا يهدي ... » has no grammatical position; it is the reason for the implied apodosis, i.e. "if you are eager for their guidance, you will not be able to, because Allah does not guide...".
And the clause «لا يهدي ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of inna.
And the clause «يضلّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
And the clause «ما لهم من ناصرين» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the causal clause.

safi-cedvel:38-39.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive [Note: or conjunctive, with the clause after it — أقسموا — conjoined to the clause: قال الذين أشركوا — verse (35) — and what lies between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined is of the kind of parenthesis.]. (أقسموا): a past verb and its agent. (بالله): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أقسموا). (جهد): an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) substituting for the maṣdar, specifying its kind. (أيمانهم): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (لا): negative. (يبعث): an imperfect verb, nominative. (الله): agent, nominative. (من): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative, direct object. (يموت): like يبعث, and the agent is a latent pronoun (huwa), which is the returning pronoun. (بلى): a particle of response affirming what was negated, i.e. "Yes, He will resurrect them". (وعدا): an absolute object of an omitted verb, i.e. "He promised that a promise". (على): a preposition, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (وعدا). (حقّا): an absolute object of an omitted verb, i.e. "it is true, truly" [Note: It is permissible for the maṣdar to be a naʿt of (وعدا), accusative like it.]. (الواو): conjunctive. (لكنّ): a particle of correction and accusative. (أكثر): the noun of lākinna, accusative. (الناس): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (لا): negative. (يعلمون): an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marker being the retention of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the agent.
The clause «أقسموا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «لا يبعث الله..» has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the oath.
And the clause «يموت ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
And the clause «لكنّ أكثر الناس ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the implied clause يبعثهم.
And the clause «لا يعلمون» is in the position of the nominative, khabar of lākinna.. And the clause (وعد) وعدا and the clause substituting for it, حقّ حقّا.. are of the kind of parenthesis, with no grammatical position.
(اللام): for causation. (يبيّن): an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; the agent is "He", i.e. Allah. (اللام): a preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يبيّن). (الّذي): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative, direct object. (يختلفون): an imperfect verb like يعلمون. (في): a preposition, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يختلفون).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يبيّن) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to the implied verb يبعثهم.
(الواو): conjunctive. (ليعلم): like ليبيّن. (الذين): a relative noun, agent. (كفروا): like أقسموا. (أنّهم): a particle of emphasis and accusative.. and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the noun of anna. (كانوا): a defective past verb, a naskh verb.. and (الواو) is the noun of kāna. (كاذبين): the khabar of كانوا, accusative, its accusative marker being the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يعلم..) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to the implied verb يبعثهم, so it is conjoined to the first interpreted maṣdar.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم كانوا ... ) is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يعلم.
And the clause «يبيّن ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
And the clause «يختلفون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذي).
And the clause «يعلم الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
And the clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين).
And the clause «كانوا ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of anna.

safi-cedvel:40-40.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما): kāffa and makfūfa (a restraining particle and what is restrained). (قولنا): mubtadaʾ, nominative.. and (نا) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (لشيء): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قولنا. (إذا): an adverb of future time, stripped of conditionality, attached to (قولنا). (أردناه): a past verb and its agent, and (الهاء) is the direct object. (أن): a maṣdar particle and accusative. (نقول): an imperfect verb, accusative; the agent is "we". (اللام): a preposition, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (نقول). (كن): a complete imperative verb; the agent is "you". (الفاء): resumptive. (يكون): a complete imperfect verb, nominative; the agent is a latent pronoun (huwa).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نقول) is in the position of the nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ قولنا..
The clause «قولنا.. أن نقول» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «أردناه ... » is in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «نقول ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
And the clause «كن ... » is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech.
And the clause «يكون» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو", i.e. "so it comes to be", and the clause is resumptive [Note: or the clause يكون.. is originally resumptive, contrary to Ibn Hishām; and see verse (117) of sūrat al-Baqara, verse (47) of sūrat Āl ʿImrān, and verse (73) of sūrat al-Anʿām.].

* Rhetoric:
- Representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): in His saying, Exalted is He, كُنْ فَيَكُونُ — it is a representation of the ease with which things within His power come about according to the attachment of His will to them, and a depiction of the speed of their coming into being by what is known from that of the obedience of the obedient one commanded to the order of the obeyed one who commands. So the meaning is: our bringing something into existence, when our will attaches to it, is only that we bring it into being in the fastest manner possible. In the verse there is a majesty and eloquence at which minds and intellects are bewildered.

* Benefits:
- «Innamā»:
Imām ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī holds that stopping, regarding «innamā», at the grammarians' statement that there is no benefit in the joining of «mā» to «inna» other than that it nullifies its operation, is a clear error, since the basis of «innamā» is that it comes for a report which the addressee is not ignorant of and does not deny the soundness of, as in His saying, Exalted is He, «إنما يستجيب الذين يسمعون», and from it is the verse of Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt:
انما مصعب شهاب من الله ... تجلّت بوجهه الظلماء
(Muṣʿab is but a flame from Allah; by his face the darkness was cleared.)
It likewise gives, for the speech that follows it, the affirmation of the action for one thing and its negation from another. So if you say: innamā jāʾanī Khālid ("Only Khālid came to me"), it is as though you said: Khālid came to me and not Saʿīd.
So you perceive with it the affirmation of the action for one party and its negation from another party, all at once.
So verify this; you have been guided to the right.

safi-cedvel:97-97.t:
* I'rab:
(من): a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ. (عمل): a past verb; the agent is a latent pronoun (huwa) referring to the conditional noun. (صالحا): direct object, accusative. (من ذكر): a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl from the agent of عمل [Note: or tamyīz (specification) of the relative noun (من).]. (أو): a conjunction. (أنثى): conjoined to ذكر, genitive, its genitive marker being the kasra implied on the alif. (الواو): the wāw of ḥāl. (هو): a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ. (مؤمن): khabar, nominative. (الفاء): linking the apodosis of the condition. (اللام): the lām of an oath, for an implied oath. (نحيينّه): an imperfect verb like نجزينّ «1», and (الهاء) is the direct object. (حياة): absolute object, accusative. (طيّبة): naʿt of حياة, accusative. (الواو): conjunctive. (لنجزينّهم أجرهم.. يعملون): like the preceding verse «2».
The clause «من عمل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «عمل صالحا ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: It is permissible for the khabar to be the two clauses of the protasis and the apodosis together.].
And the clause «هو مؤمن ... » is in the position of the accusative, ḥāl.
And the clause «نحيينّه ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the implied oath.. and the clause of the oath and its answer are the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "نحن".. and the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of the condition.
And the clause «نجزينّهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the answer to the oath.
And the clause «كانوا يعملون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the nominal or particle-relative (ما).
And the clause «يعملون» is in the position of the accusative, khabar of كانوا.

* Rhetoric:
- Completion (tatmīm): in His saying, Exalted is He, مَنْ عَمِلَ صالِحاً مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثى وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ to the end of the verse.
The tatmīm is repeated here twice. The first: in His saying, Exalted is He, مِنْ ذَكَرٍ وَأُنْثى, because the conditional or relative من gives generality, so it had to be completed with that, for emphasis and to remove the notion of restriction, in keeping with the ancient beliefs of the Arabs in preferring the male over the female and favouring him with everything that is good.
The second: in His saying وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ. Opinions differ about this tatmīm and about what is meant by the good life which one in this condition attains. The best of what we choose of them is the statement of al-Zamakhsharī in his book al-Kashshāf, and we quote it verbatim for its benefit, for he said, and excelled: "That is because the believer, together with righteous action, lives a good life, whether well-off or in straitened circumstances. If he is well-off, there is nothing to say about him; and if he is in straitened circumstances, he has with him what makes his life good, namely contentment and satisfaction with Allah's apportioning. As for the wicked, his case is the reverse: if he is in straitened circumstances, there is no difficulty in his case."

safi-cedvel:98-100.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء): resumptive. (إذا): an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, in the position of the accusative, attached to the content of the apodosis. (قرأت): a past verb and its agent. (القرآن): direct object, accusative. (الفاء): linking the apodosis of the condition. (استعذ): an imperative verb; the agent is "you". (بالله): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (استعذ). (من الشيطان): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (استعذ). (الرّجيم): naʿt of الشيطان, genitive.
The clause «قرأت ... » is in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «استعذ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(إنّ): a particle of emphasis and accusative, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of the accusative, the noun of inna. (ليس): an inert defective past verb. (اللام): a preposition, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to the khabar of ليس. (سلطان): the postposed noun of ليس, nominative. (على): a preposition. (الّذين): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the genitive, attached to (سلطان), which is in the sense of domination. (آمنوا): a past verb and its agent. (الواو): conjunctive. (على ربّهم): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يتوكّلون), and (هم) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (يتوكّلون): an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the agent.
And the clause «إنّه ليس له سلطان ... » has no grammatical position; it is the reason for an omitted element, namely the answer to the command, i.e. "seek refuge with Allah from Satan and you will be spared his evil".
And the clause «ليس له سلطان» is in the position of the nominative, khabar of inna.
And the clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين).
And the clause «يتوكّلون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
(إنّما): kāffa and makfūfa. (سلطانه): mubtadaʾ, nominative.. and (الهاء) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (على الذين): like the first, attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. (يتولّونه): like يتوكّلون.. and (الهاء) is a pronoun, direct object. (الواو): conjunctive. (الّذين): in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the preceding relative noun. (هم): a detached pronoun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ. (الباء): a preposition, and (الهاء) is in the position of the genitive, attached to (مشركون), which is the khabar, nominative, its nominative marker being the wāw.
And the clause «سلطانه على الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause «يتولّونه....» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين).
And the clause «هم به مشركون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (الّذين).

* Morphology:
(سلطان): the word is used here in the sense of domination, so it is a maṣdar. Its wazn is فعلان (ḍamma on the fāʾ).

safi-cedvel:101-101.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): conjunctive. (إذا بدّلنا آية): like إذا قرأت القرآن [Note: in verse (98) of this sūra.]. (مكان): second direct object, accusative. (آية): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الواو): parenthetical — or circumstantial. (الله): the word of majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative. (أعلم): khabar, nominative. (الباء): a preposition. (ما): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the genitive, attached to (أعلم). (ينزّل): an imperfect verb, nominative; the agent is a latent pronoun (huwa). (قالوا): a past verb and its agent. (إنّما): kāffa and makfūfa. (أنت): a detached pronoun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ. (مفتر): khabar, nominative, its nominative marker being the ḍamma implied on the omitted yāʾ, for it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ). (بل): for transitional exit (iḍrāb intiqālī). (أكثرهم): mubtadaʾ, nominative.. and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (لا): negative. (يعلمون): an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the agent.
The clause «بدّلنا ... » is in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «الله أعلم ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
And the clause «ينزّل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause «أنت مفتر» is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech.
And the clause «أكثرهم لا يعلمون» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «لا يعلمون» is in the position of the nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أكثرهم).

safi-cedvel:102-102.t:
* I'rab:
(قل): an imperative verb; the agent is "you". (نزّله): a past verb, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, direct object. (روح): agent, nominative. (القدس): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (من ربّك): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (نزّل), and (الكاف) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (بالحقّ): a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl from the agent or from the genitive second-person pronoun. (اللام): for causation. (يثبّت): an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; the agent is a latent pronoun (huwa). (الّذين): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative, direct object. (آمنوا): a past verb and its agent.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يثبّت..) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (نزّله).
(الواو): conjunctive — or circumstantial. (هدى): conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar, genitive, its genitive marker being the kasra implied on the alif [Note: or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو", and the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative.]. (الواو): conjunctive. (بشرى): conjoined to هدى, genitive like it. (للمسلمين): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (بشرى).
The clause «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «نزّله روح ... » is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech.
And the clause «يثبّت ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
And the clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).

* Benefits:
1- Returning to the hamza: we elaborated in our earlier discussion on the hamza and the rules of its writing, and since the Qur'anic orthography differs from those rules, here is the hamza of «ءامنوا», written on the line. Likewise the hamza of «ءاية», as you see, contrary to the rules we laid down for writing it. We repeat here what we said earlier, that the Qur'anic orthography is not relied upon in the orthography of ordinary writing.
2- Bal: a conjunction. If it occurs after affirmative speech, it is for iḍrāb, turning away from one thing to another, as in the verse before us.
If it occurs after a negation or a prohibition, it is for istidrāk (correction), in the position of lākin, as in: "Saʿīd did not stand, but Khalīl."
It may also be a particle of inception, if a clause follows it, as in His saying, Exalted is He: وَقالُوا اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمنُ وَلَداً سُبْحانَهُ بَلْ عِبادٌ مُكْرَمُونَ, i.e. "rather, they are honoured servants".
Abrogating and abrogated rulings in the Sharia:
The hypocrites, the weak in belief, and those in whose hearts faith had not taken hold took the abrogation of rulings as a pretext for attacking the religion and accusing the Messenger ﷺ of fabrication. Some of them would apostatise because of that.
But the intelligent and discerning person knows that the gradual introduction of rulings is a matter of wisdom, especially when the rulings of the Sharia relate to the abrogation of a deep-rooted custom or an entrenched belief, such as the drinking of wine and the change of the qibla.
Abrogation may also have some connection with the development that accompanied the stages of the conveying of the message, which led the mujtahid imams, afterwards, to lay down their principle that states:
"The change of rulings with the change of time and place is not denied."
And this is what we see as requiring the changing of man-made laws from time to time, in response to development and in keeping with the state's social, economic and intellectual condition, etc.

safi-cedvel:103-103.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive. (اللام): the lām of an oath, for an implied oath. (قد): a particle of verification [Note: because Allah's knowledge is verified, constant and continuous.]. (نعلم): an imperfect verb, nominative; the agent is "we", for exaltation. (أنّهم): a particle of emphasis and accusative.. and (هم) is in the position of the accusative, the noun of anna. (يقولون): an imperfect verb, nominative..
and (الواو) is the agent.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم يقولون..) is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of نعلم.
(إنّما): kāffa and makfūfa. (يعلّمه): an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الهاء) is a pronoun, direct object. (بشر): agent, nominative. (لسان): mubtadaʾ, nominative. (الّذي): a relative noun in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi. (يلحدون): like يقولون. (إلى): a preposition, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يلحدون). (أعجميّ): khabar, nominative. (الواو): conjunctive [Note: or circumstantial, with the clause after it as a ḥāl.]. (ها): a particle of alerting. (ذا): a demonstrative, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the Qur'an. (لسان): khabar, nominative. (عربيّ): naʿt of لسان, nominative [Note: or a second khabar, nominative.]. (مبين): a second naʿt, nominative.
The clause «نعلم..» has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the implied oath.
And the clause «يقولون ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of anna.
And the clause «إنّما يعلّمه بشر ... » is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech.
And the clause «لسان الذي ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: This is the opinion of al-Zamakhsharī; Abū Ḥayyān chose that it be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, which in his view is more forceful in rebuking them, and the pronoun in (يلحدون) is the link that ties it to the owner of the ḥāl, which is the agent of يقولون.].
And the clause «يلحدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
And the clause «هذا لسان ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause لسان الذي ...

* Rhetoric:
- Metaphor (istiʿāra): in His saying, Exalted is He, لِسانُ الَّذِي يُلْحِدُونَ إِلَيْهِ أَعْجَمِيٌّ.
Ilḥād is inclining, from alḥada al-qabr, when one makes the digging of the grave incline away from straightness, digging in a side of it; then it was borrowed for every inclining away from straightness, so they said: "So-and-so deviated (alḥada) in his speech" and "deviated in his religion".
What is meant: that is, the language of the man towards whom they incline the speech, away from straightness, is foreign and not clear.

safi-cedvel:104-104.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ): a particle of emphasis and accusative. (الذين): a relative noun in the position of the accusative, the noun of inna. (لا): negative. (يؤمنون): an imperfect verb, nominative. and (الواو) is the agent. (بآيات): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يؤمنون). (الله): the word of majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (لا): negative. (يهديهم): an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marker being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ..
and (هم) is a pronoun, direct object. (الله): the word of majesty, agent, nominative. (الواو): conjunctive. (اللام): a preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a preposed khabar. (عذاب): postposed mubtadaʾ, nominative. (أليم): naʿt of عذاب, nominative.
The clause «إنّ الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «لا يؤمنون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «لا يهديهم الله ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of inna.
And the clause «لهم عذاب ... » is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the khabar clause.

safi-cedvel:105-105.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما يفتري الكذب الّذين): like إنّما يعلّمه بشر [Note: in verse (103) of this sūra.]; the object is preposed and the agent postposed. (لا يؤمنون بآيات الله): their i'rab has been given before [Note: in the preceding verse (104).]. (الواو): conjunctive. (أولئك): a demonstrative, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ.. and (الكاف) is a particle of address. (هم): a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: or a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (الكاذبون), and the nominal clause is the khabar of the demonstrative.]. (الكاذبون): the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك.., nominative, its nominative marker being the wāw..
The clause «يفتري.. الذين..» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «لا يؤمنون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين).
And the clause «أولئك ... الكاذبون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive.

safi-cedvel:106-110.t:
* I'rab:
(من): a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ. (كفر): a past verb; the agent is a latent pronoun (huwa) referring to من. (بالله): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (كفر). (من بعد): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (كفر). (إيمانه): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (إلّا): a particle of exception. (من): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative as a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). (أكره): a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa". (الواو): circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (قلبه): mubtadaʾ, nominative.. and (الهاء) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (مطمئنّ): khabar, nominative. (بالإيمان): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (مطمئنّ). (الواو): conjunctive. (لكن): a particle of correction. (من): a relative noun [Note: It is also permissible for it to be a conditional noun, on the basis that a mubtadaʾ is implied, because a condition does not occur after istidrāk, i.e.:
"but (they are) those who opened (their breast)", and the apodosis of the condition is His saying: فعليهم غضب من الله.] indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ. (شرح): a past verb; the agent is a latent pronoun (huwa). (بالكفر): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (شرح), which is given the sense of "became content". (صدرا): tamyīz, accusative. (الفاء): redundant [Note: or it links the apodosis of the condition if (من) is parsed as a conditional noun.]. (على): a preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a preposed khabar. (غضب): postposed mubtadaʾ, nominative. (من الله): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an adjective of (غضب). (الواو): conjunctive. (اللام): a preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a preposed khabar. (عذاب عظيم): like عذاب أليم [Note: in verse (104) of this sūra.].
The clause «من كفر ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «كفر ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: It is permissible for the khabar to be the two clauses of the protasis and apodosis together.].. and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, its implied form being "then he is to be held to account.." or "then for them is a severe punishment".
And the clause «أكره ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
And the clause «قلبه مطمئنّ ... » is in the position of the accusative, ḥāl.
And the clause «من شرح.. عليهم غضب» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive.
And the clause «شرح ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (من).
And the clause «عليهم غضب ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The clause is accompanied by the fāʾ because the mubtadaʾ resembles a condition..].
And the clause «لهم عذاب ... » is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the last khabar clause.
(ذلك): a demonstrative, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the threat, (اللام) denotes distance and (الكاف) is for address. (الباء): a preposition. (أنّهم): a particle resembling the verb..
and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the accusative, the noun of anna. (استحبّوا): a past verb and its agent. (الحياة): direct object, accusative. (الدنيا): naʿt of (حياة), accusative, its accusative marker being the fatḥa implied on the alif. (على الآخرة): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (استحبّوا), which is given the sense of "preferred".
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم استحبّوا ... ) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك.
(الواو): conjunctive. (أنّ الله لا يهدي): like أنّهم استحبّوا. (القوم): direct object, accusative. (الكافرين): naʿt of القوم, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله لا يهدي..) is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the first interpreted maṣdar.
And the clause «ذلك بأنّهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause «استحبّوا ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of anna (the first).
And the clause «لا يهدي ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of anna (the second).
(أولئك): a demonstrative, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ.. and (الكاف) is for address. (الّذين): a relative noun in the position of the nominative, khabar. (طبع): a past verb. (الله): the word of majesty, agent, nominative. (على قلوبهم): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (طبع), and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو): conjunctive in the three places. (سمعهم، أبصارهم): like قلوبهم and conjoined to it by the two conjunctions. (أولئك): like the first. (هم): a separating pronoun [Note: or a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (الغافلون), and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك.]. (الغافلون): the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك.
And the clause «أولئك الّذين ... » is in the position of the accusative, ḥāl from القوم [Note: or it has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.].
And the clause «طبع الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «أولئك ... الغافلون» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause أولئك الذين طبع..
(لا جرم): a negative of generic negation, and its noun is indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of the accusative [Note: See the states of the i'rab of (لا جرم) in verse (22) of sūrat Hūd and (23, 62) of this sūra.]. (أنّهم): like the first. (في الآخرة): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (الخاسرون). (هم): a detached pronoun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ [Note: or it is a pronoun borrowed for the position of the accusative, tawkīd of the pronoun that is the noun of anna.]. (الخاسرون): khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم), nominative, its nominative marker being the wāw.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم.. هم الخاسرون) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, its implied form being "في", i.e. "no doubt in that they.. are the losers", so the preposition and its noun are attached to the khabar of lā.
And the clause «لا جرم (في) أنّهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause «هم الخاسرون» is in the position of the nominative, khabar of anna.
(ثمّ): a conjunction. (إنّ): a particle of emphasis and accusative. (ربّك): the noun of inna, accusative.. and (الكاف) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (اللام): a preposition. (الّذين): a relative noun in the position of the genitive, attached to the khabar of inna, i.e. "He is a supporter of them". (هاجروا): a past verb and its agent. (من بعد): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (هاجروا). (ما): a maṣdar particle. (فتنوا): a passive past verb.. and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil. (ثمّ): like the first. (جاهدوا): like هاجروا, and likewise (صبروا). (إنّ ربّك من بعدها): like the first.. and (ها) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (اللام): the shifted lām, for emphasis. (غفور): khabar, nominative. (رحيم): a second khabar, nominative.
And the clause «إنّ ربّك للذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause لا جرم..
And the clause «هاجروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين).
And the clause «فتنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما فتنوا..) is in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «جاهدوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause هاجروا.
And the clause «صبروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause هاجروا.
And the clause «إنّ ربّك.. لغفور» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive, to emphasise the first clause [Note: or it is a badal from the first, with no grammatical position.].

* Morphology:
(مطمئنّ): active participle of اطمأنّ, the five-letter verb. Its wazn is مفعللّ (ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the first lām).

* Benefits:
Those tried away from their religion:
- His saying, Exalted is He: مَنْ كَفَرَ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ إِيمانِهِ إِلَّا مَنْ أُكْرِهَ وَقَلْبُهُ مُطْمَئِنٌّ بِالْإِيمانِ..
When the polytheists of the people of Mecca grew severe upon the weak who had believed in what was sent down to Muḥammad ﷺ, a number of them reverted to disbelief. They were of two groups: a group that responded to the enticement of Quraysh out of fear or desire, and a group that was tortured for the sake of Allah until it was compelled to utter the word of disbelief.
Among them were ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir and his father and mother; Abū Jahl killed the two of them, and they were the first two martyrs in Islam. And among them were Ṣuhayb, Khabbāb, Bilāl and Sālim, who took refuge in precautionary dissimulation (taqiyya), so they said the word of disbelief with their tongues while their hearts were full of faith. The Messenger accepted that from them and confirmed them in it, and concerning them there was sent down of the noble Qur'an His saying, Exalted is He: إِلَّا مَنْ أُكْرِهَ وَقَلْبُهُ مُطْمَئِنٌّ بِالْإِيمانِ.

safi-cedvel:111-111.t:
* I'rab:
(يوم): direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" ("remember") [Note: or it is an adverb of time, accusative, attached to رحيم.].
