(تأتي): an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marker being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ. (كلّ): agent, nominative. (نفس): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (تجادل): an imperfect verb, nominative; the agent is "she". (عن نفسها): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تجادل), and (ها) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو): conjunctive. (توفّى): a passive imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marker being the ḍamma implied on the alif. (كلّ): nāʾib fāʿil, nominative. (نفس): like the first. (ما): a maṣdar particle. (عملت): a past verb, and (التاء) is for the feminine, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "hiya".
The interpreted maṣdar (ما عملت..) is in the position of the accusative, direct object, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the recompense of its deeds" [Note: It is permissible for (ما) to be a relative noun in the position of the accusative, with the returning pronoun omitted and the clause after it as the ṣila.].
(الواو): the wāw of ḥāl. (هم): a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ. (لا): negative. (يظلمون): a passive imperfect verb, nominative, and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil.
The clause « (اذكر) يوم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «تأتي كلّ ... » is in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «تجادل ... » is in the position of the nominative, naʿt of كلّ نفس [Note: or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.].
And the clause «توفّى كلّ نفس» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause تأتي.
And the clause «عملت ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
And the clause «و (هم) لا يظلمون» is in the position of the accusative, ḥāl.
And the clause «لا يظلمون» is in the position of the nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Morphology:
(توفّى): it has an i'lāl by substitution. Its origin is توفي — with a yāʾ at the end — the yāʾ came vowelled after a fatḥa and was turned into an alif, and it was written in the form of the yāʾ because it is the fifth letter.

* Benefits:
- يَوْمَ تَأْتِي كُلُّ نَفْسٍ:
"Kull" is a noun indicating comprehensiveness and totality, or the parts of individuals. It is either indefinite, as in كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ, or definite, as in وَكُلُّهُمْ آتِيهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ فَرْداً.
Its i'rab: it has three aspects:
The first: that it be tawkīd of a definite noun, which is the school of the Basrans.
The second: that it be a naʿt of a definite noun, indicating its perfection, as in:
«هم القوم كل القوم يا أم خالد»
(They are the people, the whole of the people, O Umm Khālid.)
The third: that it follow the governors, either annexed, as in:
كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِما كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ,
or not annexed, as in: وَكُلًّا ضَرَبْنا لَهُ الْأَمْثالَ. Among this is its standing in for the maṣdar, in which case it is accusative as an absolute object, as in فَلا تَمِيلُوا كُلَّ الْمَيْلِ; and it may be annexed to an adverb, in which case it is parsed as mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial).
Remark: the word kull is, in its ruling, singular and masculine.
The meaning of kull depends on what it is annexed to, so the meaning of what it is annexed to is observed in indefiniteness and definiteness, singular, dual and plural, masculine and feminine, as in كل نفس ذائقة الموت, وكل حزب بما لديهم فرحون, and كل نفس بما كسبت رهينة.
In all of these examples the meaning of the muḍāf ilayhi was observed and the form of "kull" was not; so reflect and act. You have been guided to the right.

safi-cedvel:112-112.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive. (ضرب): a past verb. (الله): the word of majesty, agent, nominative. (مثلا): direct object, accusative. (قرية): badal from (مثلا), accusative. (كانت): a defective past verb — and (التاء) is for the feminine — and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "hiya". (آمنة): the khabar of كان, accusative. (مطمئنّة): a second khabar, accusative. (يأتيها): like تأتي «1», and (ها) is a pronoun, direct object. (رزقها): agent, nominative.. and (ها) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (رغدا): a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl. (من كلّ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يأتيها). (مكان): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الفاء): conjunctive in the two places. (كفرت): like عملت «2». (بأنعم): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (كفرت). (الله): the word of majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (أذاقها): like عمل «3».. and (ها) is a pronoun, direct object. (الله): the word of majesty, agent, nominative. (لباس): second direct object, accusative. (الجوع): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الواو): conjunctive. (الخوف): conjoined to الجوع, genitive. (الباء): a preposition. (ما): a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of the genitive with the returning pronoun omitted.]. (كانوا يصنعون): like كانوا يعملون [Note: in verse (97) of this sūra.].
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كانوا..) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (أذاقها).
The clause «ضرب الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «كانت آمنة ... » is in the position of the accusative, naʿt of قرية.
And the clause «يأتيها رزقها» is in the position of the accusative, a third khabar of the verb كانت [Note: or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in آمنة.].
And the clause «كفرت ... » is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause كانت ...
And the clause «أذاقها الله ... » is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause كفرت..
And the clause «كانوا يصنعون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
And the clause «يصنعون» is in the position of the accusative, khabar of كانوا.

* Rhetoric:
(1) Mursal figurative usage (al-majāz al-mursal): in His saying, Exalted is He, وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا قَرْيَةً, i.e. the people of a town, the relation being locality, since the place is mentioned and what is meant is what is in it.
(2) In His saying, Exalted is He, فَأَذاقَهَا اللَّهُ لِباسَ الْجُوعِ وَالْخَوْفِ there are two implicit metaphors (istiʿāratān makniyyatān).
As for the tasting (idhāqa), it has been treated by them as literal, because of its prevalence in trials and hardships and what of them touches people; they say: "So-and-so tasted misery and harm", and "He made him taste punishment": what is experienced of the effect of harm and pain was likened to what is experienced of the taste of bitter and foul things.
As for the garment (libās), it was used as the likeness because of its enveloping the wearer: what overwhelmed a person and clung to him of certain events, as though it had surrounded them and enveloped them as a garment envelops its wearer.

safi-cedvel:113-113.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive. (اللام): the lām of an oath, for an implied oath. (قد): a particle of verification. (جاءهم): a past verb, and (هم) is a pronoun, direct object. (رسول): agent, nominative. (من): a preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to an adjective of رسول. (الفاء): conjunctive in the two places. (كذّبوه): a past verb and its agent, and (الهاء) is the direct object. (أخذهم): like جاءهم. (العذاب): agent, nominative. (الواو): the wāw of ḥāl. (هم): a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ. (ظالمون): khabar, nominative, its nominative marker being the wāw.
The clause «قد جاءهم رسول ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the implied oath.
And the clause «كذّبوه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the answer to the oath.
And the clause «أخذهم العذاب ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كذّبوه.
And the clause «هم ظالمون» is in the position of the accusative, ḥāl.

safi-cedvel:114-114.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء): linking the apodosis of an implied condition. (كلوا): an imperative verb, indeclinable on the omission of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the agent. (من): a preposition. (ما): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the genitive, attached to (كلوا). (رزقكم): a past verb.. and (كم) is a pronoun, direct object. (الله): the word of majesty, agent, nominative. (حلالا): ḥāl from the omitted second object, i.e. "Allah provided it to you" [Note: or an absolute object substituting for the maṣdar, i.e. "lawful eating", and likewise (طيّبا) .. it is also permissible for it to be a direct object, i.e. "lawful food".]. (طيّبا): a second ḥāl [Note: It is permissible for it to be a naʿt of (حلالا), accusative like it.]. (الواو): conjunctive. (اشكروا): like كلوا. (نعمة): direct object, accusative. (الله): the word of majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (إن): a jussive conditional particle. (كنتم): a defective past verb in the position of the jussive, the protasis.. and (تم) is the noun of kāna. (إيّاه): a detached pronoun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative, preposed direct object. (تعبدون): an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the agent.
The clause «كلوا ... » is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if the provision of Allah comes to you, then eat..".
And the clause «رزقكم الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause «اشكروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كلوا.
And the clause «كنتم.. تعبدون» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.. and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "if it is He whom you worship, then eat of His provision and give thanks for His favour".
And the clause «تعبدون» is in the position of the accusative, khabar of كنتم.

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab
(أتى) a past verb [[either in its basic sense, meaning "drew near".. or it is future in meaning because its occurrence is certain, as if it had occurred.]], indeclinable on the implied fatḥa on the alif. (أمر) fāʿil, nominative. (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الفاء) the linking particle of the apodosis of an implied condition [[or a conjunction linking the effect to the cause..]]. (لا) prohibitive and jussive. (تستعجلوه) an imperfect verb, jussive, its jussive marking being the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi. (سبحان) mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in genitive construct. (الواو) conjunction. (تعالى) a past verb like أتى; the fāʿil is "He". (عن) a preposition. (ما) a maṣdar particle [[or a relative noun in the position of a genitive, the returning pronoun omitted, that is "they associate with Him"]]. (يشركون) an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marking being the retention of the nūn ... and (الواو) is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما يشركون) is in the position of a genitive by the preposition, attached to (تعالى).
The clause «أتى أمر الله ...» has no grammatical position; initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «لا تستعجلوه ...» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if you demand the matter, do not hasten it".
The clause «(نسبّح) سبحانه ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «تعالى ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يشركون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the maṣdar particle (ما).

* Benefits:
1- أَتى أَمْرُ اللَّهِ: He, Glorified, expressed the future by the past, as a proclamation of the occurrence of His command and the necessity of its realisation, and this is among the subtleties of the rhetoric of the noble Qur'an, so reflect.
2- تَعالى: this verb is defective in conjugation, and it has been said: a verb, as regards conveying a meaning, either is not connected with time or is connected with it, in two kinds: inert and conjugated.
For if it is connected with time, that calls for the variation of its forms to convey its occurrence at a specific time.
And if it is not connected with time, that necessitates its being inert in one form.
Of that are hope, through the verb «عسى», blame, through the verb «بئس», and likewise praise through the verb «نعم», then wonder; all of that does not vary with the variation of time, and that is why their verbs are inert. It either keeps to the past form, like عسى, ليس, نعم, بئس, تبارك and تعالى, or the imperfect form, or the imperative form, like هب, هات, تعال and هلمّ in the language of Tamīm.
